transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I'm here because... I just have a hard time sitting still. It feels like I've got this motor humming under my skin sometimes. Like if I'm supposed to just sit and listen at a staff meeting at work, or... church briefings. I just end up shifting around a lot. Or I have to find some excuse to get up and move. That's about it.
Are you currently taking, or have you recently started, any new medications, especially any psychiatric medications like antipsychotics?
No, I don't take anything like that. Just... regular stuff. No new medications.
Thinking back, do you remember having this same restlessness and trouble sitting still as a child or teenager, or is this something that started more recently in adulthood?

No, it's... it's not new. I guess it's always been there. 

I remember getting in trouble back in grade school for it. Just... popping out of my seat. Talking over the teacher, or rushing ahead before they even finished the directions. My mother used to say I acted like I was wound too tight, even as a kid. So... yeah. It's not a recent thing.
Aside from the physical restlessness, do you also notice yourself worrying a lot or feeling anxious about different things most days?
No... not really. I don't... worry much. Just the normal stuff, I guess. Nothing out of the ordinary.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on tasks, find your mind wandering easily, or frequently lose track of things like keys or paperwork?
No, not really. I... I keep track of my stuff fine. At work, I just do what I need to do. Keep moving. So, no, I don't really lose things or... drift off.
Do you often find yourself blurting out answers or interrupting others before they finish speaking, or having trouble waiting your turn in lines or conversations?

Yeah, I guess so. Sometimes. Like... if my supervisor or someone at the church is telling me what needs doing, I... I'll just jump in. Say what I think they're getting at before they're done talking. Sometimes I'm wrong and they have to correct me. But... yeah. I do that.

Do these feelings of restlessness and jumping in before others finish talking cause problems for you in more than one area of your life—like at work, at home, and in social situations—or is it mostly limited to one setting?

Mostly just... work, I suppose. It's, uh... it's been causing some issues lately. My supervisor... well, there have been some complaints. Because I jump in, I end up missing parts of the instructions. It just creates friction, I guess, when we're doing room turnovers or... figuring out supplies. It got to the point where my boss... he pushed me to go to that employee assistance program. So... yeah. Mostly work.

Do you or people close to you—like family or friends—notice this same restlessness or impulsive interrupting happening at home or in social situations, even if it's not causing the same kind of trouble as at work?

I suppose. My wife... she brings it up sometimes. Even when we’re just trying to relax. Like if we go fishing, or... sit through bingo. I catch myself tapping, or messing with my tackle box. Or the pencil. She says I talk too loud. It just gets... hard for me to just be quiet and enjoy it, I guess.
